data.narrative:
Quantinuum, a Series G quantum computing company founded by Ilyas Khan, has raised $2.7B+ and carries a last post-money valuation of $14.8B. The comparable universe consists of three public quantum computing peers—IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), and Rigetti Computing ($4.5B)—plus four additional private-stage quantum firms including Infleqtion, representing the frontier of the sector.

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. The stage-progression method, applying a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier to the $14.8B base, implies a forward valuation of $18.5B. The peer-median method, anchoring to the median valuation of $6.3B across the three public comparables, implies $6.3B, with a range spanning $4.5B to $13.0B. These divergent signals reflect material heterogeneity in the quantum computing sector's public valuations and the uncertainty in mapping private-to-public pricing.

The triangulated range spans $5.3B (low) to $21.2B (high), with a median of $12.4B. This wide spread reflects two principal uncertainties: the degree to which Quantinuum's later stage and capital intensity justify a premium to public-market medians, and the sustainability of current quantum computing valuations amid uncertain commercialization timelines. The current $14.8B valuation sits near the median, suggesting fair pricing relative to stage peers, though comps themselves remain volatile.
